chunks: I say the truth, and call the moon to witness,

key_terms.كَلاَّ: An emphatic particle meaning 'Nay' or 'Indeed', used to affirm the following statement.
key_terms.وَالْقَمَرِ: The moon, the object of the divine oath in this verse.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the oath by the moon in Surah Al-Muddaththir?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-Muddaththir, Allah swears by the moon (Al-Qamar) to underscore the absolute certainty of the resurrection and the reality of the Hereafter, a theme central to the Meccan period's emphasis on accountability. Shia exegetes often highlight this oath as a rhetorical device to capture the attention of the Quraysh, who were familiar with lunar cycles, thereby affirming the Prophet's mission against their skepticism. This verse serves as a powerful divine affirmation that the message conveyed is not mere poetry or magic, but a clear truth from the Lord of the worlds.
